model_drafts.title: Arbitrary code execution via eval() on user-controlled input
model_drafts.explanation: eval() parses and executes its string argument as Python code in the current global and local namespace. Here the string is taken directly from input(), so anything a user types is executed with the privileges of the running process. findings.title: Arbitrary code execution via eval() on function argument
findings.explanation: run() passes its parameter 'code' directly to eval(), which parses and executes it as Python source in the current scope. If any caller supplies data that originates from an untrusted source (HTTP request, file, CLI arg, message queue), an attacker can execute arbitrary Python in the process, leading to data disclosure, file/system modification, or full host compromise. The actual exploitability depends on unseen callers, so this is a dangerous sink rather than a confirmed end-to-end vulnerability.
